purpose: Test whether a disciplined score-level blend of frozen BGE-M3 hybrid first-stage scores and BGE-reranker-v2-m3 cross-encoder scores improves Arabic MIRACL dev retrieval.
research_basis: MIRACL Arabic nDCG@10 is the strongest current retrieval benchmark signal in this repo.
The current v47 system uses a strong two-stage stack but discards first-stage score information after reranking.
A tune/holdout split is required because score blending on the same dev set can overfit.

method.candidate_source: v47 BGE-M3 hybrid r100 plus BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 ranked_by_query.json

grid.alpha_definition: alpha * reranker_score + (1 - alpha) * first_stage_score after per-query normalization for minmax/zscore; alpha=1.0 is reranker-only.

interpretation: The selected min-max blend improves on the v47 reranker-only system on both tune and holdout halves, so the gain is not limited to the tuned half.
The full-dev score is the strongest completed Arabic MIRACLRetrieval dev result in this repo: 0.828605 nDCG@10.
This remains a retrieval-system result over MIRACL dev, not a standalone Arabic embedding model and not a formal hidden-test SOTA claim.
next_experiment: Run full-dev BGE-reranker-v2-gemma over the same v43 candidate pool, then repeat the blend sweep with Gemma scores if the full run beats or approaches v56.
